What makes Protoceratops so amazing?

About the size of a sheep, Protoceratops is a small herbivore dinosaur—an ancestor of horned dinosaurs like Triceratops. It's also very famous for its egg fossils.

content.text:
Nature and science facts about Protoceratops

Protoceratops lived about 75 million years ago in the deserts of Mongolia and China. Its eggs took about 83 days to hatch, and each egg was around 20cm long. Its eyeballs were about 5cm across—twice the size of human eyes. Thanks to those big eyes, it probably saw well even in dim places. Nests and egg fossils were found together, which helped us greatly in understanding how dinosaurs reproduced.

Points worth exploring together

Point out things like its small size (about like a sheep), its big eyes, the eggs and nest, and its desert life. Talking about "How many days did the eggs take to hatch?" together is a great way to spark curiosity.

Parent guide — how to grow curiosity

Use your hands to picture the 20cm egg size, and compare it with a chicken egg. Find Mongolia on a map, and comparing "It saw well with its big eyes" to an owl makes it even more interesting.

Frequently Asked Questions (FAQ)

Q. How big were Protoceratops eggs?
A. About 20cm long, and they took around 83 days to hatch. Nest fossils were found together with them.

Q. Were its eyes big?
A. Yes. Its eyeballs were about 5cm across—twice the size of human eyes. It probably saw well even in dim places.

Q. How can we enjoy it at home?
A. Picturing the 20cm egg size, comparing it with a chicken egg, and finding Mongolia on a map are all great.
